chapters.title: Partakers of the Divine Nature
chapters.html:
2 Peter 1

Greeting

1Simeon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained a faith as precious as ours by the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ:

2grace and peace be multiplied to you in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.

Make Your Calling Sure

3His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness, through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and excellence.

4Through these He has given us His precious and very great promises, so that through them you may become sharers in the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world because of desire.

5For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith excellence, and to excellence knowledge,

6and to knowledge self-control, and to self-control endurance, and to endurance godliness,

7and to godliness brotherly affection, and to brotherly affection love.

8For if these things are yours and are increasing, they keep you from being idle or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

9Whoever lacks them is blind, shortsighted, having forgotten that he was cleansed from his old sins.

10So, brothers, be all the more eager to make your calling and election sure, for if you do these things you will never stumble.

11In this way there will be richly provided for you an entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

The Prophetic Word

12So I intend always to remind you of these things, though you know them and are established in the truth you have.

13I think it right, as long as I am in this tent, to stir you up by way of reminder,

14since I know that the putting off of my tent will be soon, as our Lord Jesus Christ made clear to me.

15I will make every effort that after my departure you may be able at any time to recall these things.

16For we did not follow cleverly invented myths when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.

17For He received honor and glory from God the Father when the voice was borne to Him by the Majestic Glory: "This is My Son, My beloved, in whom I am well pleased."

18We ourselves heard this voice borne from heaven, for we were with Him on the holy mountain.

19We have the prophetic word made more sure, and you will do well to pay attention to it as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts,

20knowing this first of all, that no prophecy of Scripture comes from one's own interpretation.

21For no prophecy was ever brought by the will of man, but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.

Notes

  • v1 "our God and Savior Jesus Christ" — tou theou hēmōn kai sōtēros Iēsou Christou, one article over both nouns, as in v11, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, where the two titles name one person. Read so, Jesus Christ is called our God and Savior; read with God and Savior as two, the righteousness is of God and of Jesus Christ. v2 names the two apart: the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.

  • vv15–18 "after my departure… on the holy mountain" — exodos, departure, the word of the mountain where Peter saw Jesus' glory: Moses and Elijah spoke of His departure, which He was about to fulfill in Jerusalem (Luke 9:31). The voice he heard there, This is My Son, the beloved, in whom I am well pleased (Matthew 17:5), is the one he quotes. Tent (vv13–14) is his body, which he will soon put off.

  • v20 "no prophecy of Scripture comes from one's own interpretation" — idias epilyseōs, of one's own unloosing. One's own may be the prophet's: no prophet made up the meaning of what he saw, for men spoke from God (v21). Or it may be the reader's: no one is to read prophecy by his own private sense of it.

chapters.title: False Teachers
chapters.html:
2 Peter 2

False Teachers Among You

1There were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you. They will secretly bring in destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them, bringing swift destruction on themselves.

2Many will follow their sensuality, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed.

3In their greed they will exploit you with made-up words. Their condemnation from long ago is not idle, and their destruction is not asleep.

4For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them down to Tartarus and handed them over to chains of gloom, to be kept for judgment;

5if He did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, a herald of righteousness, one of eight, when He brought a flood on the world of the ungodly;

6if He condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to destruction, reducing them to ashes and making them an example of what is coming for the ungodly;

7and if He rescued righteous Lot, worn down by the sensual conduct of the lawless

8(for as that righteous man lived among them day after day, he tormented his righteous soul over the lawless deeds he saw and heard);

9then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment,

10especially those who follow the flesh in polluting desire and despise authority. Bold and willful, they do not tremble as they blaspheme the glorious ones,

11whereas angels, though greater in strength and power, do not bring a blasphemous judgment against them.

12But these people, like unreasoning animals, creatures of instinct born to be caught and destroyed, blaspheme about matters they do not understand, and in their destruction they will also be destroyed,

13suffering wrong as the wage for their wrongdoing. They count it pleasure to revel in the daytime. They are blots and blemishes, reveling in their deceptions while they feast with you.

14They have eyes full of adultery, never ceasing from sin. They entice unsteady souls. They have hearts trained in greed. Children of a curse!

15Leaving the straight way, they have gone astray, following the way of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the wage of wrongdoing,

16but was rebuked for his own transgression: a speechless donkey spoke with a human voice and restrained the prophet's madness.

Worse Than at the First

17These people are springs without water and mists driven by a storm. For them the gloom of darkness has been reserved.

18For, speaking loud words of emptiness, they entice by sensual desires of the flesh those who are barely escaping from the people who live in error.

19They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for whatever overcomes a person, to that he is enslaved.

20For if, after they have escaped the defilements of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome, the last state has become worse for them than the first.

21It would have been better for them never to have known the way of righteousness than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment handed down to them.

22What the true proverb says has happened to them: "A dog returns to its own vomit," and, "A sow, after washing, returns to wallow in the mud."

Notes

  • v4 "cast them down to Tartarus" — tartarōsas, a verb made from Tartarus, the deepest pit beneath the world in Greek speech, and found only here in the New Testament. 1 Enoch names it in the Greek: Uriel is over the world and over Tartarus (1 Enoch 20:2), in the book that tells how the angels who sinned were bound in darkness until the day of the great judgment (1 Enoch 10:4–6, 12). Jude says the same of them (Jude 6).

  • vv15–16 "Balaam son of Bosor… a speechless donkey spoke" — Numbers names him Balaam son of Beor (Numbers 22:5); the edition prints Bosor here. The LORD opened the donkey's mouth (Numbers 22:28), and the beast that cannot speak stops the prophet who was paid to curse.

  • v22 "A dog returns to its own vomit" — Proverbs 26:11, in this canon Reproof (Tegsat) 2:11: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly. The sow is not from any book of the Old Testament.

chapters.title: The Day of the Lord
chapters.html:
2 Peter 3

Where Is the Promise?

1Beloved, this is now the second letter I am writing to you, and in both I am stirring up your sincere mind by way of reminder,

2to remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets and the commandment of the Lord and Savior through your apostles,

3knowing this first of all, that in the last days scoffers will come with scoffing, following their own desires

4and saying, "Where is the promise of His coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of creation."

5For they willfully overlook this: that long ago, by the word of God, heavens existed, and an earth formed out of water and through water,

6through which the world of that time was flooded with water and perished.

7But by the same word the heavens and earth that now exist are stored up for fire, kept for the day of judgment and destruction of the ungodly.

A Thousand Years as One Day

8But do not overlook this one thing, beloved: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.

9The Lord is not slow to fulfill His promise, as some count slowness, but is patient toward you, not wanting anyone to perish, but all to come to repentance.

10But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a roar, the elements will be burned up and dissolved, and the earth and the works done on it will be found.

11Since all these things are to be dissolved in this way, what sort of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness,

12waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be set on fire and dissolved, and the elements will melt as they burn!

13But according to His promise we are waiting for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.

Grow in Grace

14So, beloved, since you are waiting for these, be eager to be found by Him without spot or blemish, at peace.

15Count the patience of our Lord as salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given him,

16as he does in all his letters when he speaks of these things. There are some things in them hard to understand, which the ignorant and unstable twist, as they do the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.

17You therefore, beloved, knowing this beforehand, be on your guard, so that you are not carried away by the error of the lawless and fall from your own firm footing.

18But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.

Notes

  • v8 "one day is like a thousand years" — Psalm 90:4, a thousand years in Your sight are like yesterday when it is past. Peter turns the line both ways: a thousand years are as a day, and a day as a thousand years.

  • v10 "the earth and the works done on it will be found" — heurethēsetai, will be found, as the edition prints it. The same verb in v14 is to be found by Him: the earth and its works will be found out, laid open before God, when the heavens pass away. The mark beside the word shows that copies read differently here.

  • v13 "new heavens and a new earth" — Isaiah 65:17, I am about to create new heavens and a new earth, and 66:22.
